text:
Predicates:
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
DepositRequired(x) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in x.
DepositAmount(x, y) ::: The security deposit for x is y.
Rent(x, y) ::: The monthly rent at x is y.
Owns(x, y) ::: x owns y.
Cat(x) ::: x is a cat.
WillRent(x, y) ::: x will rent an apartment in y.
Allowed(x, y) ::: x is allowed to move in with y.
Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(pets, x)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → DepositRequired(x)) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → (DepositAmount(x, oneMonthRent) ∨ DepositAmount(x, moreThanOneMonthRent))) ::: The security deposit can be either equal to one month's rent or more.
Cat(fluffy) ∧ Owns(tom, fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat.
∀x (Cat(x) → Pet(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
Rent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
∀x (ManagedBuilding(x) → (WillRent(tom, x) ↔ (Allowed(tom, fluffy) ∧ DepositAmount(x, y) ∧ y ≤ 1500))) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
2000 > 1500 ::: 2000$ is more than $1500.
Conclusion:
WillRent(tom, oliveGarden) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in The Olive Garden.
